articleBody:
- [ ] Breaker panel verified — Turn off electrical circuits feeding kitchen counters before outlet covers are removed for safety.
- [ ] Countertop cleared and covered — Protect stone or laminate counters and flooring from falling tools and wet mortar drops.
- [ ] High-grease zones degreased — Clean cooking splatter behind the stove with a heavy-duty cleaner so thinset bonds securely.
- [ ] Drywall repairs completed — Patch deep gouges and ensure studs or drywall boards are flat across the entire span.
- [ ] Outlets and switches evaluated — Identify whether box extenders or longer screws will be needed once tile thickness is added.
- [ ] End points measured — Mark precise ending lines at upper cabinet edges and window casings to avoid awkward partial cuts.
- [ ] Trim pieces on site — Verify matching pencil tile or metal edge trim pieces are present before the first row begins.
- [ ] Waste allowance verified — Confirm you ordered 10 to 15 percent extra tile to cover cuts, breakage, and future wall repairs.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through your kitchen with this list before installation begins. Addressing wall flaws and electrical safety in advance prevents delays once adhesive is mixed.
